eigenfaces: The first three components describe the largest training-set variations; the last three shown describe much smaller residual variations. In this run, PC1 shows a recognizable face outline with eye and mouth contrast, PC2 has a broad left-to-right brightness contrast, and PC3 emphasizes the face silhouette against its surroundings. PC148-PC150 contain finer alternating patches around facial structures rather than a single broad lighting pattern. These are visual interpretations of the plotted components, not identity labels; the sign of an eigenvector is arbitrary.
failure_analysis: These failures were selected programmatically from unequal true and predicted labels. In the displayed first row, the Blair-to-Bush error has an open mouth and an upward-looking pose; the Bush-to-Powell error has pronounced side lighting; the two Rumsfeld-to-Bush errors show glasses and different face crops/angles. In the second row, the Bush-to-Powell image at the second position has a downward head tilt and a strong shadow. Expression, pose and illumination can change global pixel coefficients more than identity differences, so they are plausible contributors. These are image-specific hypotheses, not proven causes; no causal experiment was performed. A linear PCA subspace summarizes global pixel variation and may confuse identity with illumination or pose.
